protocol: Post-hypobaric-hypoxia-training presentation. Figure 1, p. 85, illustrates routine training at 25,000 ft with 30 minutes of prescribed 100% oxygen before ascent. Patient-specific altitude, pressure schedule and delivered oxygen are unreported.
outcome_window: Symptom onset after the training. Exact onset interval, time to first assessment and post-treatment follow-up are unreported.
locator: Case and Discussion, printed pp. 85–86 (PDF pp. 97–98)
note: The 26-year-old woman reported air hunger. ECG showed sinus tachycardia and arterial blood gas showed hypoxia, hypocarbia and mild respiratory alkalosis. CT angiography did not show pulmonary thromboembolism. The team treated provisional DCS with hyperbaric oxygen and considered the diagnosis confirmed after symptoms resolved. The authors attributed inadequate denitrogenation to mask fit on case review. Delivered FiO2 and the exposure denominator are unavailable.
